items.impact: The artifact is a closed JSON object whose production-exclusion contract is expressed through three top-level fields.
items.statement: The production wiring exclusions artifact is structurally a single JSON object containing generation metadata, an exclusion-token array, and a reason string.
items.title: Production exclusions manifest root

items.impact: These 31 exact strings are the complete declared production-wiring exclusion set in this artifact and therefore define the immediate exclusion input consumed downstream.
items.statement: The manifest enumerates 31 excluded command tokens, including literal namespace roots, concrete command identifiers, and two entries containing a trailing wildcard marker.
items.title: Declared excluded-token set

evidence.exact_quote: "reason": "Excluded from production wiring JSON because token is a parser artifact, invalid historical alias, generic family root, or compatibility-only namespace root. Web capability production commands are canonical under cmd.chat.web.*; cmd.web.* rows are compatibility-only and must not hide active chat, NL, palette, or agent-routed web capability."

items.impact: Compatibility-only cmd.web.* rows are barred from suppressing active web entry points across chat, natural-language routing, palette routing, and agent routing.
items.statement: The manifest explicitly establishes cmd.chat.web.* as the canonical production namespace and treats cmd.web.* rows as compatibility-only without permitting those rows to hide active web capability.
items.title: Canonical web namespace protection

evidence.exact_quote: "reason": "Excluded from production wiring JSON because token is a parser artifact, invalid historical alias, generic family root, or compatibility-only namespace root. Web capability production commands are canonical under cmd.chat.web.*; cmd.web.* rows are compatibility-only and must not hide active chat, NL, palette, or agent-routed web capability."

items.impact: A validator or maintainer cannot prove which exclusion category applies to any token, distinguish intentional compatibility retention from a parser artifact, or detect category drift without making an undocumented judgment.
items.statement: The single reason string supplies four possible exclusion categories but does not bind an individual excluded token to one category or to token-specific evidence.
items.title: Per-token rationale is absent

items.impact: Different consumers may interpret the asterisk literally, as a glob, or as a prefix selector; the resulting under-exclusion or over-exclusion could silently change production capability visibility.
items.statement: The artifact contains wildcard-like token strings but defines neither the token grammar nor exact-match, prefix-match, escaping, normalization, duplicate, ordering, or malformed-value behavior.
items.title: Token matching semantics are undefined

items.impact: A timestamp alone cannot establish which generator, inputs, policy version, or repository state produced the exclusions, nor whether regeneration succeeded atomically or the file is stale.
items.statement: The manifest records only a generation timestamp and supplies no generator identity, input digest, policy or schema version, freshness rule, regeneration transition, rollback behavior, or provenance oracle.
items.title: Generation provenance and lifecycle are unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: "reason": "Excluded from production wiring JSON because token is a parser artifact, invalid historical alias, generic family root, or compatibility-only namespace root. Web capability production commands are canonical under cmd.chat.web.*; cmd.web.* rows are compatibility-only and must not hide active chat, NL, palette, or agent-routed web capability."

items.impact: The no-hide guarantee cannot be falsified from this artifact, and consumers could apply exclusions at inconsistent pipeline stages or fail open or closed without any declared detection, recovery, or rollback behavior.
items.statement: The artifact does not name its owner, callers, consumers, enforcement stage, authority, propagation path, concurrent update behavior, partial-failure policy, recovery mechanism, or executable oracle for the stated no-hide requirement.
items.title: Enforcement ownership and acceptance oracle are missing

items.impact: Because exclusions span operationally sensitive and user-visible command families, an implementation may accidentally equate absence from production wiring with denied authority, hidden capability, or safe deprecation even though this artifact defines none of those meanings.
items.statement: The manifest does not establish whether exclusion affects discoverability only, executable authority, GUI visibility, data lifecycle, destructive-action safeguards, or some combination of these concerns.
items.title: Authority and user-surface consequences are unknown

segments.summary: Reviewed all 37 core lines and all nine assigned source units. The artifact clearly enumerates exclusions and protects canonical cmd.chat.web.* behavior, but leaves token matching, per-token rationale, generation provenance, enforcement ownership, lifecycle, authority effects, and executable acceptance oracles undefined.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner defines exclusion matching, enforcement stage, consumers, failure policy, and the distinction between unwired, hidden, deprecated, and unauthorized commands?
Which canonical wiring and GUI contracts prove that compatibility-only cmd.web.* rows cannot hide active chat, natural-language, palette, or agent-routed web capability?
